defects.claim_says: The conditions imported from the Cotton Textile approval are incorporated as they stood and add no end of their own; no held record shows an earlier end, so the first end is 1935-06-14.
defects.source_says: Held EO 6206 (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6206-code-fair-competition-for-the-cotton-textile-industry.txt, July 16, 1933) records that the Cotton Textile approval of July 9, 1933 carried 'condition 12 of said order providing for the termination of approval at the end of four months unless expressly renewed', withdrawn only on July 16, 1933 and only for the Cotton Textile code. EO 6204-A (July 14, 1933) approved the Rayon Weaving provisions 'subject to the interpretations and conditions imposed by me on my approval of the corresponding provisions of said Cotton Textile Code', so as they stood on July 14 the imported conditions included a four-month termination. The claim neither addresses this possible own-terms end (about November 1933, unless renewed or unless the July 16 withdrawal carried over) nor records it as a gap.

Whether the imported four-month termination condition applied to this partial approval, and whether any renewal or later Rayon Weaving action followed (the July 9 order and any renewal are not held), is a material open question on the first end. The parallel partial approval of the Throwing Industry the same day (EO 6204-B) was followed by a full approval (EO 6331-E, WPA p. 543), which shows interim approvals of this form were superseded; for Rayon Weaving none is held, which is absence of evidence, not proof.

defects.claim_says: A held later order, Executive Order 6513 of December 18, 1933, approves "an Amendment (Number I)" to this code
defects.source_says: The amendment is Executive Order 6513-I (APP heading 'Executive Order 6513-I—Code of Fair Competition for the Cast Iron Soil Pipe Industry (Amendment Number I)'; WPA list '6513-1: Dec. 18 Amendment to the Code...'). Executive Order 6513 (no suffix) of the same date is a different order, 'Amendment of Executive Order No. 6433-A' (Special Industrial Recovery Board / National Emergency Council; WPA p. 557).

defects.claim_says: A held later order, Executive Order 6885 of October 25, 1934, approves an amended code for the Builders Supplies Trade
defects.source_says: The amending order is Executive Order 6885-A of October 25, 1934 (APP heading 'Executive Order 6885-A—Amended Code of Fair Competition for the Builders Supplies Trade'; WPA p. 594 '6885-A'). Executive Order 6885 is a different order of October 23, 1934 amending rules for the Army and Navy General Hospital, Hot Springs, Arkansas.

defects.claim_says: Executive Order 6925 of December 19, 1934, which places the construction operations of the Cinders, Ashes, and Scavenger Trade under it
defects.source_says: The order is Executive Order 6925-A of December 19, 1934 (APP heading 'Executive Order 6925-A—Canceling Order Approving Code for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade'; WPA p. 598). Its operative command cancels the order approving the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade code; only its recital states that upon cancellation the construction operations 'will be subject to' the Construction Industry code. Executive Order 6925 is a different order of December 18, 1934 (Tongass National Forest land restoration).

defects.claim_says: "Approval recommended: Hugh S. Johnson, Administrator" is a recommendation, not a command.
defects.source_says: Held EO 6875 text has no 'Approval recommended' line; it ends 'FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT / The White House, / October 16, 1934.'

defects.claim_says: the recitals describe the application, hearings and the Administrator's findings and command nothing
defects.source_says: Recital: application for amendment 'and in order to carry out the recommendations of the Board of Inquiry for the Cotton Textile Industry, created by Executive Order No. 6840'; no hearings or Administrator's findings recited

defects.claim_says: the WPA 1944 list entry for 1934 Oct 16, p.593, records the code for the Silk Textile Industry as approved
defects.source_says: WPA p.593: 'Amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Silk Textile Industry approved. XVIII NRA Codes 207.'

defects.claim_says: No held order after October 16, 1934 names the Cotton Textile Code.
defects.source_says: EO 6878 (October 16, 1934) and EO 6930 (December 27, 1934), held in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts, are each issued 'under the Codes of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile Industry, the Silk Textile Industry and the Wool Textile Industry'. EO 6878 directs the Cotton Textile Work Assignment Board on work assignments (the stretch-out), and EO 6930 extends EO 6878's January 1, 1935 deadline for that board's recommendations.
